To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the geographic perspective and spatial thinking are important in promoting community engagement and in building and sustaining a reciprocal relationship between the university and community.

1) geographic CBLR can be used to develop a sense of community and a shared identity, 2) geographic CBLRs can be used to build and sustain reciprocal relationships between the university and the community, 3) geographic CBLRS can be used to foster civic engagement, and 4) the use of geographic CBLR in interdisciplinary contexts can be used to promote interdisciplinary research, teaching, and community engagement.
the impacts of geographic CBLR transcend the boundaries of geography, and that geographic perspectives and methods can contribute to the theory and practice of civic engagement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which geographers can contribute to the development of civic engagement in the university and beyond.
the ways in which geographers are able to intervene in the theory and practice of CBLR.
the development and use of spatial thinking and mapping to support and enhance the community engagement process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the role of geography and geographers in community engagement is to promote a critical spatial thinking that is inclusive of all stakeholders and is grounded in the community's own needs and priorities.
geography can play a significant role in promoting community engagement, but that geographers have not yet realized the potential that geography holds for community engagement.
the discipline of geography can and should play a key role in the promotion of civic engagement in higher education.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a community-based geographic research course that has been effective in teaching students about community engagement while also providing a service to our community.
we have been able to demonstrate how geographic and spatial thinking can help to foster community engagement and community partnerships.
we are working to build a more inclusive community through geographic and interdisciplinary CBLR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

geographic and interdisciplinary community-based learning and research can help students, community partners, and faculty learn about each other, and in the process, develop a deeper appreciation and understanding of the community and the university.
geographic CBLR can help students and communities to think about their own place in the larger context, which is the core of geographic thinking and practice.
geography is a unique discipline in its ability to facilitate community based learning and to foster civic engagement through its spatial thinking and methods.
